y-m-37-10.title: Two numbers wey sum na 10: how big product fit be?
y-m-37-10.topic: Whether two numbers with given sum and product fit dey, and compare two methods of solving
y-m-37-10.goal: Use condition for real roots of quadratic equation to work out whether two real numbers with given sum and product fit dey, then compare how strong evidence from table wey only get integers be with expression wey handle all real numbers.
y-m-37-10.material: Make p and q be two real numbers wey sum na 10, and their product pq na P. Two friends use different methods to check whether such real numbers dey when P given. Gaeun: make p = t and q = 10 − t, then check whether t(10 − t) = P, that is, t² − 10t + P = 0, get real root t. Narae: change t to 0, 1, 2, … and make table of products. Narae table (t, 10 − t, product): (0, 10, 0), (1, 9, 9), (2, 8, 16), (3, 7, 21), (4, 6, 24), (5, 5, 25), (6, 4, 24), (7, 3, 21).
y-m-37-10.thinking.0: Compare the evidence behind the two solving methods
y-m-37-10.thinking.1: Make the existing cases fit the conditions yourself
y-m-37-10.thinking.2: Explain say e impossible using evidence
y-m-37-10.prereq.1: Discriminant of quadratic equation and whether real roots dey
y-m-37-10.prereq.2: Relationship between roots and coefficients, or completing the square
y-m-37-10.s.s1.prompt: Choose the explanation wey best compare the two methods on whether two real numbers fit get product 26.
y-m-37-10.s.s1.hint.0: Separate t values wey dey in Narae table from those wey no dey.
y-m-37-10.s.s1.hint.1: Choose one t wey no be integer (for example, 5.5), calculate product yourself, and compare am with table shape.
y-m-37-10.s.s1.o.a: Both methods reach same conclusion, so Narae table by itself enough.
y-m-37-10.s.s1.r.a: Even if conclusions same, evidence strength different. Narae table only get integer t values.
y-m-37-10.s.s1.o.b: 26 no dey table, so Narae method wey show products directly more reliable.
y-m-37-10.s.s1.r.b: The fact say 26 no dey table na result of checking integer t only. Decimal t cases no dey in the table.
y-m-37-10.s.s1.o.c: You fit use Gaeun method only when P na integer.
y-m-37-10.s.s1.r.c: You fit use t² − 10t + P = 0 the same way even when P na decimal or fraction. You fit calculate discriminant for any real P.
y-m-37-10.s.s1.o.d: Table handle integer t only, but Gaeun expression handle every real t.
y-m-37-10.s.s1.explain: Narae table only handle integer t, so e no fit settle say 26 impossible. But the shape, wey symmetric and biggest at 5, na good clue say 25 maximum. Gaeun expression handle every real t, so e fit settle am by whether discriminant 100 − 4P negative.
y-m-37-10.s.s2.prompt: Find 3 different integer P values wey two different real numbers fit get sum 10 and product P, and those numbers no be integers.
y-m-37-10.s.s2.hint.0: First find the P range wey make discriminant of Gaeun expression t² − 10t + P = 0 positive.
y-m-37-10.s.s2.hint.1: For some integer P in that range, find the two numbers yourself and check whether dem integers.
y-m-37-10.s.s2.fail.c2: Use Gaeun expression to work out which range product must dey before two different real numbers with sum 10 fit exist.
y-m-37-10.s.s2.ok.c3: The two numbers no be integers.
y-m-37-10.s.s2.fail.c3: Really find both numbers for that P and check whether dem integers.
y-m-37-10.s.s2.explain: The roots of t² − 10t + P = 0 na t = 5 ± √(25 − P). If P < 25, two different real numbers dey; and if 25 − P no be perfect square, dem no be integers. P = 24 give 4 and 6, wey be integers; P = 25 give only 5; and P = 26 no get real numbers.
y-m-37-10.s.s3.prompt: Wetin evidence you need before you fit say two real numbers with product 26 no dey? Choose Gaeun or Narae method and write the evidence, plus how strong that method evidence be for this question.
y-m-37-10.s.s3.hint.0: Calculate discriminant of t²−10t+26=0 and check the sign. Or rewrite t(10−t) in a way wey get (t−5)² inside.
y-m-37-10.s.s3.hint.1: Write one sentence about wetin Narae table show and wetin e no fit show.
y-m-37-10.s.s3.selfAssess.0: With the method wey I choose, I use numbers or expression show why product 26 no possible?
y-m-37-10.s.s3.selfAssess.1: I talk about how certainty differ between 'table wey check integers only' and 'expression wey handle all real numbers'?
y-m-37-10.s.s3.model.0: With Gaeun method, discriminant of t² − 10t + 26 = 0 na 100 − 104 = −4, wey negative, so no real root t dey. So no real numbers with sum 10 and product 26 dey. The method handle every real t, so evidence strong.
y-m-37-10.s.s3.model.1: t(10 − t) = −(t − 5)² + 25, so product no fit pass 25. So 26 no fit happen. Narae table get integers only, so e hint say 25 maximum but no fit settle am.
